key_insight: An agentic, stateful AI workbench—the "AI co-mathematician"—helps mathematicians run long-horizon, exploratory research by coordinating AI agents that manage uncertainty, refine intent, and remember failed hypotheses. It turns fragmented single-turn assistance into a continuous, reproducible research partner.
problem_solved: Mathematical research is open-ended, iterative, and requires tracking evolving intent, failed experiments, literature, computations and proofs over long timescales; existing single-turn AI tools cannot maintain the state, provenance and coordination needed for sustained discovery.
method: An asynchronous, stateful workspace that stores history, hypotheses, and provenance so work can be resumed, reviewed and iterated.
Agentic AI components that collaborate on distinct tasks (ideation, literature search, computational exploration, theorem proving, theory building) and refine user intent over time.
Uncertainty-management and failure-tracking mechanisms to record, revisit and learn from failed hypotheses and partial results, improving efficiency of exploratory loops.
impact: Provides a practical platform to accelerate mathematical discovery and reduce cognitive overhead, making long-horizon research workflows more reproducible and collaborative. For AI/ML practitioners, it demonstrates scalable agent coordination, stateful interaction design, and evaluation paradigms for complex, open-ended tasks.
visual_elements: A workflow diagram showing the human researcher interacting with multiple AI agents inside a central stateful workspace (arrows for asynchronous task flow).
A timeline or swimlane chart illustrating tracked hypotheses, failed attempts, and iterative refinements across sessions.
Icon row for core capabilities: Ideation, Literature Search, Computational Exploration, Theorem Proving (simple icons with short labels).
A provenance snapshot mockup showing saved notes, code runs, proofs, and links to sources to highlight reproducibility and state.
paper_title: AI Co-Mathematician: Accelerating Mathematicians with Agentic AI
paper_authors: Daniel Zheng, Ingrid von Glehn, Yori Zwols, Iuliya Beloshapka, Lars Buesing
